review_type: Scoped retrospective literature review; not a systematic review
questions: What counts as meaningful improvement beyond a molecular readout?
What practical work would intervention, follow-up and everyday care ask of people?
How do understanding, information barriers and stigma shape communication?

sources.author: DiBenedetti DB et al.
sources.title: Assessing what matters most to patients with or at risk for Alzheimer’s and care partners: a qualitative study evaluating symptoms, impacts, and outcomes
sources.sample: 60 interview units across five AD-continuum groups; 12 per group; moderate-stage group included 12 patient–care-partner dyads; severe-stage reports came from care partners
sources.time: Published 30 July 2020; fieldwork dates not established in the inspected methods
sources.finding: Memory, disease progression and independence were important desired outcomes.
sources.checked: Study population, interview methods, Tables 1, 2, 6 and 7, discussion and funding
sources.limit: Clinical referrals; stage-specific and proxy perspectives; qualitative mentions are not population preferences. Industry-supported consortium.
sources.reason: Connects biological evaluation to daily-life outcomes without specifying an ORCA clinical endpoint.

sources.author: Wang M et al.
sources.title: The needs of informal caregivers and barriers of primary care workers toward dementia management in primary care: a qualitative study in Beijing
sources.setting: Four community health service centers, Chaoyang district, Beijing
sources.sample: 10 informal-caregiver interviews; focus groups with 29 primary care workers
sources.time: Caregiver interviews September–December 2017; worker groups January–February 2018; published December 2018
sources.finding: Care knowledge, psychological support and collaborative management emerged alongside staff workload barriers.
sources.checked: Recruitment, data collection, results themes, participant tables and limitations
sources.limit: Small purposive urban district sample; not a nationwide needs estimate.
sources.reason: Adds direct Chinese caregiver and service perspectives to care-center and implementation reflections.

sources.author: Li Y et al.
sources.title: Factors Associated With Alzheimer’s Disease Patients’ Caregiving Status and Family Caregiving Burden in China
sources.setting: Health-center recruitment across 30 mainland Chinese provincial-level regions
sources.sample: 1,675 valid questionnaires concerning people with probable AD; completed by family or professional caregivers with staff guidance
sources.finding: Family care predominated in the recruited sample; care burden varied with care context and self-care ability.
sources.checked: Design, inclusion criteria, data collection, Table 1, care-burden tables and limitations
sources.limit: Non-probability health-center sample, predominantly urban; education criterion over five years; cross-sectional associations.
sources.reason: Makes family time and service capacity relevant without predicting ORCA burden.

sources.author: Dranitsaris G et al.
sources.title: Therapeutic preference for Alzheimer’s disease treatments: a discrete choice experiment with caregivers and neurologists
sources.sample: 180 caregiver and 179 neurologist completers; 137 and 161 retained after attention/comprehension exclusions
sources.time: Published 24 March 2023; fieldwork dates not established in the inspected text
sources.finding: Both groups valued clinical benefit and safety; their weighting of administration and titration differed.
sources.checked: Methods, seven attributes, exclusion flow, Tables 2–3, Figures 2–3 and discussion
sources.limit: Hypothetical amyloid-targeting treatment choices; costs and quality-of-life gains held equal; no patient self-report. Eisai funded.
sources.reason: Preserves stakeholder disagreement; supplies questions, not transferable RNA-editing risk tolerances.

sources.author: Alzheimer’s Disease International
sources.title: World Alzheimer Report 2024: Global changes in attitudes to dementia
sources.type: Official report with original international survey
sources.sample: 34,619 answered at least one stigma-related item: 789 people with dementia, 10,605 carers, 8,797 health/care professionals and 14,428 general-public respondents
sources.time: 2024 report; exact survey field dates not established in inspected methods
sources.finding: The normal-ageing misconception and stigma remained concerns across respondent groups.
sources.checked: Original PDF chapter 2, pages 27–28 and methodology/sample pages 55–56; Table 1 page 64 is missing weights, not country sample size
sources.limit: Convenience/snowball and targeted recruitment, weighted analyses, item-specific denominators and demographic imbalance; global results are not Shenzhen estimates.
sources.reason: Distinguishes wider dementia beliefs from ORCA’s technology-information questionnaire.

sources.author: US Food and Drug Administration
sources.title: Patient-Focused Drug Development: Collecting Comprehensive and Representative Input
sources.type: Methodological guidance, not a patient-needs study
sources.finding: Define the population and reporter, favor direct patient input when feasible, and document sampling and missingness.
sources.checked: Sections II.B–F, printed pages 9–19; Figure 1 and sampling tables
sources.limit: Not empirical evidence of local needs, not an ORCA regulatory pathway or a completed team method.
sources.reason: Supports a better plan for future target-population engagement.
